newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran warns Gulf states with close foreign ties.
newsitem.headline: Iran warns Gulf states with close foreign ties.

text.p: Iran on Sunday warned Gulf Arab states with close ties with foreign powers that they would be the first to "burn" if the region became instable.
Spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who nine days ago warned Washington against attacking Iran, issued the warning to the Gulf states in a sermon marking the Moslem Eid al-Fitr feast.

"If this region should become insecure the very same countries that have prepared the conditions for that insecurity will bear the brunt of their action, for having offered their soil to them (foreign troops)," the official Iranian news agency IRNA quoted Khamenei as saying.

"If any of these foreign powers should indulge in a lunatic act in the Persian Gulf and put the region into chaos because of an irrational act, the first state that will burn in the fire will be the very same state which has created the conditions for the presence in the Persian Gulf of that foreign power."

Iran has rejected media reports that it was linked to the bombing of a U.S. military complex in Saudi Arabia in June that killed 19 American airmen. Some Tehran officials have said the reports indicated that Washington was preparing to attack Iran.
Gulf Arab states have increasingly looked to the United States for protection from potential security threats from Iran and Iraq since the 1991 Gulf War.
Half a million mostly American soldiers landed on Saudi soil to launch attacks on Iraqi troops during the Gulf War that ended Iraq's seven-month occupation of Kuwait.
Washington accuses Tehran of supporting international terrorism, a charge denied by Iran which has tried to improve ties with Gulf Arab states.

Khamenei reiterated Iranian charges that the United States was trying to stoke regional tensions in order to maintain a military presence in the oil-rich region and sell weapons to its Gulf Arab allies.
"He said the Persian Gulf states would be wiser to watch out that foreign forces might not put the Persian Gulf into a chaotic condition," IRNA said.

In a Friday prayer sermon on January 31, Khamenei said the United States was spreading "rumours" that it was going to attack Iran. Any such strike, he said, "would only make this nation more steadfast and increase its enmity towards America and the Zionists (Israel)", he added.
